## 2. Two different "$299" hypotheses — do not merge them

1. **Live catalog Signal**: $299 per **month**, recurring B2B SaaS team subscription (3 brand workspaces, 100 questions, weekly cadence per /pricing copy). Exists in Paddle; not approved for sale.
2. **2026-10-11 Commercial Investment Report**: $299 per **four-week single-client pilot** aimed at 2–20-person SEO/GEO agencies (per prior Chat08 checkpoint reading of that report; the report itself was not available in this session).

They have different buyers, scope, delivery hours and renewal semantics. Table A models (2); Table B models (1). The Stage-0 constitution (`docs/STAGE-0-CUSTOMER-PROOF-90-DAY.md`, issue #283) models a third: $3,000/$6,000 assisted pilots (Table D). A founder disposition is required before any offer.

## 3. Model formula check

- `fourWeekPilotScenario` (existing, 50d64a93) re-derived by hand for 1 client: 299 − (14.95 + 0.50) fees − 2.99 refund reserve − 12 provider − 6 h × $25 = **$118.56**; CAC 2 h × $25 + $20 = $70; minus $100 fixed = **−$51.44**. Matches Table A and the regression test.
- New `cohortScenario` with one period, no churn, reproduces the single-period helper exactly (test `cohort scenario reproduces single-period helper`), so the multi-period stress uses the same formulas.
- Paddle fee input 5% + $0.50 per checkout transaction — https://www.paddle.com/pricing (read 2026-10-13). Paddle is merchant of record, so tax is collected by Paddle and is outside these figures. Payout schedule/threshold and FX were **not** verifiable by API; settlement lag is a stress input (0–1 period).
- `Financial_Model_36_Months.csv`: the earlier Chat08 run (2026-10-12) reported tracing it to `Startup_Decision_Report.md` §11 (Supplier Quote Review, $199/$299/$399 ARPA) with 0 arithmetic discrepancies over 108 rows. **That file was not available in this session** (not in the package, repo, or any branch) so the check could not be re-run here. Disposition unchanged: it is another business's model and is **not applied** to Foremention.

## 4. Free vs paid and quota boundaries (from current repo/peer state, not new decisions)

- Free/beta: 10 approved buyer questions (public /pricing copy; enforced by verified-entitlement capacity per Chat03 status). Planned Core 25 / Signal 100 questions apply only with a verified paid entitlement.
- Provider spend: Chat06 capacity model uses a $5/org-month cap and $0.10/question reservation (CODE), expected $1.48 and worst-case $3.29 per org-month at weekly cadence. Free-only Workers AI mode gives $0 provider spend but neuron quotas become the binding limit (Chat01/A18 to measure).
- A single-client pilot in Table A is bounded at a hypothetical 60 provider calls; this is a scenario parameter, not a runtime permission.
- Founder review time binds first (Chat06: ~32 h/month at 20 orgs on weekly cadence). Table C shows the same with Chat08 assumptions: at 4 h recurring per client, an 80 h/four-week founder delivery capacity (20 h/week hypothesis) is breached at ~17 active clients while still onboarding and selling (base case, period 9), and 20 steady-state clients alone would consume all 80 h.

## 6. Reading the stress tests

- Table A ($299 four-week agency pilot) is only marginally positive after CAC at 5 clients and needs 160 founder hours per four weeks at 20 clients; it cannot scale without cutting recurring hours well under the CV-13 4 h ceiling. Its "margin" is dominated by imputed founder labor at an assumed $25/h.
- Table B (Signal/Core subscriptions) looks better only because Chat06's 1.6 h/org/month review assumption is far lower than Table A's 6 h. That assumption is **unmeasured**. The first real service-time log (template `templates/service-time-log.csv`) replaces it.
- Table C: churn, collection and recurring-hour overruns move outcome far more than fees. Settlement lag changes cash timing, not contribution. Capacity, not cash, is the first wall in every case where recurring time ≥ 4 h.
- Table D: an assisted $3k/$6k pilot tolerates 56–226 founder hours before going negative, but the hours are not known and must be logged from the first engagement.
- Pilots are never MRR: `recurringRevenueRunRateUsd` excludes each client's first (pilot) period by construction, and `summarizeCommercialProof` always returns `mrrCents: null`.

## 7. Unknowns that block a real model

Measured founder minutes per client and category; actual paid acceptance at any price; churn/continuation after an elapsed period; Paddle payout timing and successful first payout; FX/currency of customers; refund/chargeback rate; real acquisition channel conversion and time (CV-16); infrastructure plan changes (Workers Paid, Supabase plan, backups per Chat06).
